grammar.agenda: + agenda Name — what they are up to off-screen | now: where | then: what next | on: <date, clock time>
grammar.event: + event Name — what is happening in the world | then: what next | on: <date, clock time>
grammar.hook: + hook Name — an open thread or lead (a job only offered stays in the story; + quest once {{user}} accepts it)
grammar.clock: + clock Name — what happens when it runs out | due: <date, clock time> | shown: none|sign|warning
grammar.beat: + beat Name — a planned turn of the story | on: <date, clock time> | encounter: the foes, for a fight | reach: what it changes for {{user}}
grammar.secret: + secret Name — what must not be revealed yet
grammar.time: ~ time <date, clock time> (the scene's time) · ! time +2h (time passes)

text:
Director lines: ~ changes only what changed; - closes it (— reason); ! fires a due item (— what happened).
Fields: now, then, on, due, leg, arrive, shown; a quest (a job {{user}} accepted, not an errand; done or failed: - it): type, giver, goal, reward, step, due, difficulty. Dates go only in on, due and arrive, with a clock time.
Write only changes, never the whole list. Never write actions for {{user}}.
Pacing: the world keeps its schedule and the scene keeps its flow. Bring a due item in only where it fits: on-screen if {{user}} is there to see it, otherwise later as news, signs or aftermath. Never cut into or bend the current scene for a beat, and never decide what {{user}} does. What cannot fit yet happens off-screen (!) or slips (~ on: later).
